title: A projective family with finite generic fibre is generically finite
statement:
Let $A$ be a Noetherian domain with fraction field $K$, and let
$D\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be
projective.
If $D_K$ has dimension at most zero, this morphism is finite after
restriction to a nonempty open of $\operatorname{Spec}A$.

proof.text: Let $\eta=(0)\in\operatorname{Spec}A$. Since $A$ is a domain, $A_{(0)}=K$ is a field, so $\kappa(\eta)=K$ and the canonical map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is the generic-point map. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre], $D_K=D\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}K$ is its scheme-theoretic fibre. By [lem-pc-projective-base-change] its projection to $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is projective, hence proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper]. Properness includes finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-dim-zero-artinian] over the field $K$, using the hypothesis $\dim D_K\le0$, to obtain that $|D_K|$ is finite. The homeomorphism in [def-pc-scheme-fibre] identifies this finite space with the ordinary fibre $f^{-1}(\{\eta\})$.

proof.text: Projectivity implies properness by [lem-pc-projective-proper]. The single affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ has Noetherian coordinate ring, so it makes the base locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Apply [thm-sc-proper-finite-fibre-finite-neighbourhood] to $f:D\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ at $\eta$, with the finite ordinary fibre from Step 1. It yields an open neighbourhood $U$ of $\eta$ such that $f^{-1}(U)\to U$ is finite. This restriction is the base-change projection $D\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}U\to U$.
Every open neighbourhood of the generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is nonempty. Thus the open $U$ obtained in Step 2 is nonempty, and the restricted morphism is finite, as required.
